items.statement: Every OSFP record MUST carry osfpVersion, recordType, and an id that is never reused.
Every timestamp in an OSFP record MUST be an RFC 3339 date-time in UTC, written with the offset Z.
A producer MUST NOT change an OSFP record after writing it; a change of state is a new record with a new id.
A consumer MUST ignore fields it does not recognize, and MUST reject a record whose osfpVersion it does not support.
A consumer MUST NOT treat a status or state value it does not recognize as success.
A consumer MUST reject a record that reuses a known id with different content.
A factory MUST record a task grant before it dispatches any attempt of that task.
A grant's approvedBy MUST name the person who approved it, or the person who approved the standing grant it derives from.
A factory MUST NOT treat a request, an instruction, a skill, or a tool listing as a grant of authority.
A grant MUST list every resource, operation, disclosure, and tool it permits, and a factory MUST deny any that the grant does not list.
Before each side effect it performs or relays, a factory MUST confirm that the task's authority permits that side effect, and MUST NOT perform it otherwise.
A derived grant MUST NOT permit anything that its standing grant does not permit, MUST keep each of the standing grant's restrictions, and MUST NOT have a longer limit or a later expiry.
For each restriction in a grant, a factory MUST record whether it is enforced or only conveyed to the harness as an instruction, and MUST NOT record an instruction as enforced.
Each disclosure in a grant MUST name its source, its revision, and its destination.
A factory MUST NOT place a credential in a model's input.
A factory SHOULD keep credentials out of reach of code that a model writes, for example behind a proxy outside the harness's sandbox.
A factory MUST persist an attempt's attemptId before it dispatches the attempt to a harness.
An outcome MUST be in exactly one of these states: admitted, started, waiting, completed, failed, canceled, rejected, or unknown.
A factory MUST NOT record started until the harness acknowledges the attempt; admitting an attempt is not starting it.
When a factory cannot establish whether an attempt ran or what it changed, it MUST record the state unknown.
While an attempt is unknown, a factory MUST NOT start another attempt of the same task until a person approves a new grant for the task whose unknownAttempts names that attempt.
When a factory sends a command to a harness again, it MUST reuse the command's original identity, and MUST NOT reuse that identity for a different command, or once the harness may no longer hold it.
A factory MUST record a stop as three separate facts, each with its own time: stop requested, stop confirmed, and cleanup confirmed.
A factory MUST NOT record cleanup as confirmed until every process, container, and volume the attempt created is gone; the exit of a lead process does not confirm cleanup.
Verification evidence MUST be an in-toto Statement whose subject identifies the checked tree by a gitTree or dirHash digest.
Each check in the evidence MUST report exactly one status: passed, failed, not-run, or incomplete.

A check MUST NOT report passed unless its command exited with its success status, it examined at least one unit, and every unit it examined passed; skipped, deselected, and expected-failure units are not examined.
A check MUST record the exit status of the command that ran it, not the status of a command that read its output.
If a check's output was cut off, or the tree's digest changed between the check's start and its end, the check MUST report incomplete.
If an attempt changed a test, a grader, an assertion, or other code or configuration that decides a check's result, other than the code the check judges, the evidence MUST say so for that check.
If an attempt could read expected answers or a reference implementation that a check compares against and that were withheld from the attempt, the evidence MUST say so for that check.
Findings from static analysis SHOULD be recorded in SARIF 2.1.0 and referenced from the evidence by digest.
Evidence SHOULD be signed in a DSSE envelope.
A factory MUST NOT accept as verification evidence any text that a model wrote, or any evidence that the attempt could have produced or altered.

A consumer MUST NOT count a check as passed unless its evidence says that the attempt did not change what decides the check's result and could not read its withheld answers, or a person decides it may.
A factory MUST record each verdict with a reference to the evidence it reviewed, and MUST NOT change the status of any check because of a verdict.
A grant MUST state, for each attempt, a deadline for the harness to acknowledge the start and a total time budget.
A supervisor MUST run the timer that enforces an attempt's limits in a process separate from the one that runs the attempt.
When a limit expires, a supervisor MUST request a stop of the attempt.
A supervisor MUST report a scheduled task as missed when no started event arrives within startAckSeconds of its expected start, and as unfinished when a started task does not end within totalSeconds.
A factory MUST send a started event for each attempt of a scheduled task when the harness acknowledges the attempt.
An ended event for an inspection task MUST carry a result, and that result MUST be aborted, never clean, if the task inspected nothing.
Every progress record MUST name its event in event, and the time the event happened in occurredAt.
Progress events SHOULD be sent as CloudEvents.

A factory that runs harnesses through UHP MUST map each UHP task, together with the continuations that answer its input requests, to exactly one OSFP attempt, and MUST keep the attempt's attemptId after the harness stops retaining the idempotency key.

When a grant provides a tool from an MCP server, the grant MUST name the server by an identifier that the factory assigns and keeps unique, not by the name the server reports, and the tool by its name.
A factory that reports outcomes over A2A MUST map each OSFP state to A2A as the mapping in section 11 shows, so that unknown becomes TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED and never a terminal state.

A factory that reads A2A tasks MUST map each A2A state to OSFP as the mapping in section 11 shows, and MUST treat a task as unknown when its state is missing, unspecified, or unrecognized, or when its metadata gives the OSFP state unknown.
A factory that reports outcomes over A2A SHOULD carry each outcome's OSFP state in the task's metadata, under the key io.github.sunnypatneedi.osfp.state.
Traces of an attempt SHOULD use OpenTelemetry and SHOULD carry the OSFP task and attempt identifiers as attributes.
